statement: Every claim this block makes, the code path that carries it, the result that shows it, the mutation that would break it, and where it is written down. A row without a negative mutation says so; a row that is still open says so.

rows.claim: The bus reconnects to an ActiveMQ broker that really went away, on both protocols.
rows.codePath: ActiveMqHostConfiguration.ReceiveTransportRetryPolicy drives the reconnect; the relay in front of the broker keeps the address stable across the restart.
rows.negativeMutation: ReceiveTransportRetryPolicy set to Retry.None: both cases red with 'the receive endpoint never became ready again after the broker returned'. An earlier mutation on ReceiveEndpoint.IsUnrecoverable changed nothing, which is recorded as a finding about that probe.

rows.claim: DeployPublishTopology makes the ActiveMQ broker hold the topics of the named types.
rows.codePath: ConfigureActiveMqTopologyFilter.Declare resolves the topic and calls SessionContext.Materialize, which opens and closes a producer inside the session executor.
rows.testResult: four cases read the broker through Jolokia, all green; the whole category 154 of 154 with no exclusion and no [Explicit]
rows.negativeMutation: the filter resolves without materializing, which is the old behaviour: three assertions red naming the type that was not deployed

rows.claim: publish-load reports a complete run only when every published identity arrived exactly once.
rows.codePath: PublishLoadScenario.SequenceLedger keeps the expected set; completion is every sequence seen once.
rows.testResult: 2000 messages, complete true, uniqueConsumed 2000, nothing missing or duplicated
rows.negativeMutation: sequence 1 never published and sequence 0 published twice, same total: complete false, uniqueConsumed 1999, missing [1], duplicates [0], no rate reported
rows.evidence: record-0090/write-census.json names the scenario; the run outputs are in the record

rows.claim: Two runs on one machine share nothing.
rows.codePath: run_broker_category.py derives one identity per run; the compose project and the run root under artifacts/run-output follow from it.
rows.testResult: two runs started at the same moment against different brokers, both exit 0, distinct identities and roots, zero containers left
rows.negativeMutation: a run killed while its fixture was up leaves exactly one container named after its own project and touches neither the other roots nor the other containers

rows.claim: A fixture that could not be removed does not produce a green run.
rows.codePath: stop() reads the compose exit code and raises TeardownError; main re-raises it when nothing else had already failed.
rows.testResult: two cases, one for the failure and one for the success
rows.negativeMutation: the ignored exit code put back: 'TeardownError not raised'

rows.claim: Every project of this repository is classified exactly once and every required job is explained.
rows.codePath: build/verification/VERIFICATION_MODEL.json, checked by tools/ci/verification_model.py in both directions.
rows.testResult: 41 of 41 projects classified, 10 required runs declared, policy green
rows.negativeMutation: an invented job, a run naming the wrong project, a workflow job no capability explains, a floor lowered to zero - four cases; disabling the bidirectional half turns the third red

rows.claim: A test never makes the checked-out repository truth unavailable.
rows.codePath: tools/identity/test_change_list.py splits reading cases from cases that own their repository.
rows.testResult: two simultaneous identity suites both exit 0, 99 cases each, CHANGELIST.md byte identical
rows.negativeMutation: the previous version put back byte for byte fails one of the two with FileNotFoundError on CHANGELIST.md

rows.claim: Directory.Build.targets enforces the central contract rather than decorating the root.
rows.codePath: five error-raising targets hung off real build targets
rows.testResult: the file is in the evaluated graph of a directly built project; VOSB0005 fires for netstandard2.0 without the compiler host marker; VOSB0001 fires for a restore with the lock file off
rows.negativeMutation: three policy cases refuse a file with no target, a target that hangs off nothing, and one that only warns

rows.claim: The SQL fixture runs on a supported image.
rows.codePath: compose.yaml pins mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest by digest with its platform declared.
rows.testResult: the fixture becomes healthy on this arm64 machine under emulation and the SQL transport category passes 110 of 110
rows.negativeMutation: not applicable - this is a substrate replacement, and the measurement is whether the substrate carries the existing proofs unchanged

rows.claim: The local tool manifest binds the tools this repository uses.
rows.codePath: none - no dotnet tool is referenced anywhere in the repository
rows.testResult: census over every markdown, workflow, python and project file: nothing matched
rows.state: open, and deliberately: any manifest would either be empty, which section 7 forbids, or add a tool to the frozen dependency contract, which section 7 says is a question before the edit

unresolved: The local tool manifest binds the tools this repository uses.
